items.text: The file format and the legend: the binding says how the file is read and written, and its template holds the legend; DESL only names the binding.
The looks taken from the Knowledge designer: DESL's surface names which types play which part and what the page's layout is, not how a host draws a tag, a menu or a list.
items.reason: How a tag, a menu or a list is drawn, in the host's theme, fonts and controls, is rendering; the description names the colours (enum Colour) and the parts the surface's members play.

items.text: Which gesture starts which operation: the table above.
items.reason: The pointer and the keys are mapped by the host onto the intents the description names, one operation per gesture.

hostCode.behaviour: A file the binding cannot read (no envelope, not UTF-8) opens as an empty, read-only page with the one reason.
The last item number and the last requirement number given are read from the mark line, line 2.
ITEM-NEW and REQ-NEW are given the next number in memory only: one more than the higher of the mark and the highest number written, counted apart per kind, in reading order.
An entry's parent is the item it is nested in; a category and a state are read on requirements only; the title, the description and the tags come from the binding's rules.
An entry is collapsed when the registration's collapsed block holds `<number>: yes`.
An assessment's id is `assessment/<n>` by its place; its kind is read in any case and a ticked checkbox means resolved.
A list's members are its registration block's when there is one, else the initial members; the names entries carry that no member has are implicit members, spelt as first seen, coloured `default`.
A stored column width is used only for a depth of 1 or more and a width of 120 to 2000 pixels; any other column has the host's width.
An entry with an empty title is reported by std.required.
A requirement at the top level, and anything nested in a requirement, is reported by std.containment.
A number in square brackets that names no entry, in a description or an assessment's number, text or detail, is reported by std.mentions at its line.
std.missingId and std.mentions are warnings, fbl.unknown-block is information, every other finding an error.
A list's members come first and the values only entries carry follow; a member's id is `tag/`, `category/` or `state/` and its name in lower case.
A new document is the binding's template with the file's base name as its title, and no registration.
Every edit of the body writes the number of each placeholder and raises the mark of each kind it numbered, adding the mark line when it is missing.

A new top item goes last at the top level, a new sub-item last in its item, an entry added below directly after its target, and a new requirement after the item's last requirement or before its first sub-item.
A moved item or requirement goes after the sibling named; without one, to the front of its kind within its own item, or where a new one would go in another item.
A move of an item into itself or into anything it contains is refused, as is a requirement moved to the top level.
Deleting an entry removes its bullet with everything nested in it.
A new assessment goes at the end of Assessments, about the entry's number, a question unless another kind is given, and open.
Changing an assessment sets its kind, text and detail; resolving switches it; removing deletes its bullet.
A typed name is trimmed and its spaces written as `-`; names compare ignoring case.
Adding a tag picks the member of that name in any case, with the list's spelling, or creates it last in the list; removing a tag removes it ignoring case.
Renaming a tag renames it on every entry that carries it, deleting it removes it from them, in the same step.
Setting a category or a state writes a member's name; renaming or deleting a member renames or clears it on every requirement that carries it.
Collapsing writes or removes `<number>: yes` in the registration's collapsed block, outside the undo history; an entry without its own number is collapsed on the page only.
Storing, renaming and removing a filter write the registration's filters block only.
A change to a list or a filter creates the registration when the document has none.
The filter field reads `#tag`, `category:name`, `@state`, `item:pattern` and `sort:key` words; words of one kind are alternatives and kinds combine; narrowing writes nothing.
Requirements sort by number, title, or a member's place in its list, a requirement without the value last.
An edit made against a file whose bytes differ from those the page was read from is refused, and the file is read again.
hostCode.reason: Detecting a file another program changed and keeping one consistent history across writers is the host's file handling and undo stack; a description states each edit as splices with an exact undo.

hostCode.behaviour: Undo gives back the exact bytes of every file of the step; when a file changed since, the history is dropped.
hostCode.reason: Each transaction's one step with its exact undo is the description's; keeping and dropping the stack across steps and outside writes is the host's.

hostCode.behaviour: A file changed outside is read again, up to three times 20 ms apart while it cannot be read, keeping what is collapsed by number.
hostCode.reason: Watching files and re-reading them after another program writes is the host's; reading itself is the binding's.

hostCode.behaviour: Ctrl+Enter adds an item or a requirement below the selected one, Ctrl+Shift+Enter a requirement in the selected item.
hostCode.reason: Keys are mapped by the host onto the operations addItemBelow, addRequirementBelow and addRequirement, which the description states.

hostCode.behaviour: Dragging an item by its grip onto the lower half of another places it after, onto the upper half into it; a requirement goes after or before another; the drop sends moveItem or moveRequirement.
hostCode.reason: The pointer gesture is the host's; what it does is the operations moveItem and moveRequirement.

hostCode.behaviour: Delete asks first when the entry holds anything or a text or an assessment names it.
The page shows as many levels as fit its width, marks deeper levels that do not fit, and focuses on any item with a trail back.
hostCode.reason: How many levels fit and how focus is drawn is the host's drawing of DESL's hierarchy surface, which the description names with `surface hierarchy`.

hostCode.behaviour: An entry shows the icon of the kind of its one open assessment, an icon with a count for several, and a collapsed item counts everything inside it.
hostCode.reason: The icons are the enumeration AssessmentKind's; drawing them and counting is the host's drawing of the surface's notes.

hostCode.behaviour: Tags, categories and states are drawn as rounded labels in their member's colour, the Knowledge designer's looks.
hostCode.reason: The companion leaves the looks to the host: colours as theme tokens, typography and the shape of a label.

hostCode.behaviour: The page's title is the file's first `# ` heading, else the file name without its extension.
hostCode.reason: The title shown above the page is chrome the host draws; the heading is unbound text the binding keeps.
